text:
maria.dev: Heads-up — seeing a sharp p95 east-west latency spike during the 12:30-12:45 batching window, mostly rack-7 GPU nodes. graphs show step-like jumps, packet retransmits up.
jon.eng: Is this RDMA path or TCP? any packetloss vs reorder?
kevin.sre: Can you paste the pcap or a tcpdump snippet? also check if any kube rollout happened around then.
maria.dev: attaching quick tcpdump excerpt from 10.20.7.* -> lots of dup acks then cwnd backoff:
```
12:31:02.123456 IP 10.20.7.12.60234 > 10.20.7.29.1025: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12410, ack 9876, win 512
12:31:02.124000 IP 10.20.7.29.1025 > 10.20.7.12.60234: Flags [F.], seq 9876, ack 12345, win 256
12:31:02.124050 IP 10.20.7.12.60234 > 10.20.7.29.1025: Flags [.], ack 9876, win 128 (duplicate ack)
```
maria.dev: Also seeing transient ARP cache clears on the ToR logs around 12:14 and 12:28.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: batch-optimizer/v2.1 rolled to rack-7 (nodes 7-12) at 2024-08-15T12:14:33Z.
jon.eng: hmm rollout + ARP churn could explain neighbor table flushes and re-learning cost. did the rollout touch node NIC drivers or CNI?
kevin.sre: I checked the kube events — a daemonset update for bpf-conntrack went out at 12:13. that can evict kernel state if it's reloading maps.
samuel.ml: ML load also had a spike — large warmup prompt / long sequences increased KV cache misses at the same time, so more inter-node chatter. could be a perfect storm.
kevin.sre: Quick mitigation: temporarily cordon noisy pod and scale down the batch workers on rack-7, toggle ECMP to src-dst hashing on the ToR if possible. disabling GRO/GSO on affected NICs also helped earlier for reorder issues.
maria.dev: tried cordon+drain of one worker, p95 dropped ~20% but still noisy. ran `ethtool -k eth0` and toggled rx-gro-offload off, then p95 improved another notch.
jon.eng: Any RDMA QP resets? run `rdma-smi` and check QP errors.
kevin.sre: rdma-smi shows 0 QP errors. looks primarily TCP path. also saw a brief netfilter conntrack surge in kernel log: `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping`.
maria.dev: that conntrack full event lines up with the bpf-conntrack rollout — maps were resized but during reload we briefly hit capacity.
oncall: @oncall taking this — can we put a temporary rota to avoid big rolling updates during lunch batching windows?
samuel.ml: Agree — we'll add a gating rule on the CI job so daemonset rollouts won't happen during 12:15-12:50 PDT for production racks.
kevin.sre: Follow-ups: 1) increase conntrack map size slightly, 2) add preflight check in daemonset job to ensure map resize applied before reload, 3) schedule ECMP hashing tweak and monitor, 4) run a controlled iperf3 test across rack-7 during next lunch window.
maria.dev: created GH issue #5847 with logs and graphs, and added playbook notes for disabling GRO, cordon, and checking conntrack. thanks all. :thumbsup:
jon.eng: leaving notes: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and `ip link set dev eth0 gro off` as temporary steps in the runbook.
kevin.sre: I'll own the follow-up change to the daemonset CI and schedule a dry-run next Tue during maintenance window.
maria.dev: marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if it pops next lunch.
